property_summary: When transfer to an empty _tos array is not reverted, the reference returns true but the buggy version returns false.

When the external call in transfer() fails (returns false), the original contract reverts the entire transaction, while the mutated contract returns true despite the failure, so a subsequent call to a view getter (balanceOf) will be reachable only in the mutant.

When the external call in transfer() succeeds but returns false (e.g., the token's transferFrom returns false without reverting), the reference reverts the transaction while the mutant returns true; after calling transfer() with a call that returns false, calling a simple getter succeeds in the mutant but is blocked by revert in the reference.

When an external call to a token contract's transferFrom returns false (without reverting), the original contract reverts the entire transfer while the mutant returns true; after such a call, checking the contract's balance reveals the mutant succeeded whereas the reference reverted.

When transfer() calls an external contract that returns false without reverting, the reference reverts the transaction but the mutant returns true, so after the call a view function succeeds only for the mutant.
Call transfer() with a token that returns false on transferFrom (without reverting); reference reverts, mutant returns true, so a balance check after the call is reachable only in the mutant.

When caddress.call fails (e.g., token contract reverts), reference contract reverts whole transaction (outputs false) while buggy contract ignores failure and returns true; test calls transfer with a failing token call and asserts transfer(address,address,address[],uint256) returns false.
Call transfer with a single valid recipient and value 1; the reference returns true, whereas the mutant reverts due to require(false).
